Donald Trump makes things up every day - about war, the economy, his deal-
making prowess. But nothing captures his compulsion for fabulism better than
golf.

Early this month, Trump
[announced](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117027337618143949)
on social media that he shot a two-under-par 70 at his Bedminster NJ course to
win another of his "40 Club Championships." The 80-year-old president boasted:
"It's called TALENT, and I have it."

Golf aficionados immediately recognized something else, called "cheating."
Conservative journalist Scott McConnell, a Trump club member who has seen him
play often,
[posted](https://x.com/ScottMcConnell9/status/2084004157459947922?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2084004157459947922%7Ctwgr%5E3c66366f5a0a7e80d418f2cc69ab426dfa259d4e%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.hitc.com%2F2600602-2%2F)
on X: "No one like that can win a senior club championship in any universe."

"No 80-year-old on earth with a pancake swing and the chip yips has ever shot
TEN SHOTS under his age,"
[added](https://x.com/ReillyRick/status/2084301994710458460) golf writer Rick
Reilly, an authority on the president's game. The title of Reilly's book on
the subject: _Commander in Cheat_.

Millions of American golfers, trying to make their rounds a bit more
respectable, take mulligans every weekend. It's a harmless indulgence. What
distinguishes Trump - a more than respectable golfer - is the extent of his
cheating, not just on the course but in every realm of life.
